correctness.rationale: For \(1\le a<b<c\), the unique \(1^c\), \(0\,1^a\,0\) and \(0\,1^b\,0\) factors force one long-run marker and the shared zero. The factors \(1^{a+1}0\) and \(1^{a+1}0\,1^{a+1}\) prove \(c-a\le j\le a+1\). The complement of any candidate pair has two explicit arcs, each containing at most one zero; checking pure-one and one-zero factors suffices for all circular factors. When this interval is empty the explicit three-point witness gives a matching upper bound. The separately implemented literal factor-mask census checked all \(220\) triples with \(c\le12\) and the second direct-occurrence method rechecked those with \(c\le7\). Finite computations are not substituted for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The three-marker circle is the first natural sparse-marker case in which unequal independent gap lengths can force an alphabet-size-two circular attractor to require three sites. The theorem completely classifies its generic pairwise-distinct gap regime, identifies a sharp nontrivial transition \(c=2a+1\), counts every optimal pair in the two-phase region, and shows total independence from the middle gap. It is a parametric infinite-family result rather than an arbitrary finite lookup or a restatement of a recognition algorithm.
